raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Add three construction-time Platform hooks so out-of-tree backends can adapt fused MoE routers, routed experts, and runners without replacing `FusedMoEFactory`. Default platform behavior and upstream selection priority stay unchanged.

Related: #51005. This updates the existing PR; the open-PR duplicate checks found no other implementation of these construction hooks. EPLB lifecycle and transfer hooks remain separate in #49700.

## Claims

- Adapt the class already selected by the factory or model, including explicit model-specific expert loaders and runners.
- Accept compatible sibling router constructors and validate all returned components against their common contracts.
- Add no platform lookup, synchronization, or state management to the forward path. Explicitly supplied router instances remain directly usable.

## Validation

Conflict repair on 2026-11-04: rebased onto `5225a1f17f9cf721efd5ad793e6b63798ca30306`; current head `26076835a9e3b4d47d5eaeffe6c482cb1f6cd5aa`. Preserved the main-branch nullable device argument and the non-contiguous-routing regression test alongside the three construction hooks. `git range-diff` shows only the changed main-branch context; the hook behavior is unchanged.

Current-head validation: 7 focused platform tests and 31 routing-simulator tests passed on CPU; all applicable pre-commit hooks on the five changed files and `git diff --check` passed. The CPU routing normalization was also compared with main, and the shared custom-router stride rejection was checked. A fresh NPU run could not start because the remote validation environments were unreachable. Hosted CI must validate this new head.

Earlier validation below was collected at `9d551d17355aad5c7dc02746fb70528549b188f8` on base `9bc1c8b4fede8d009b308fecf74e560a1b4f7eca`; hardware and model results are historical evidence, not fresh runs of the current head.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Focused platform regressions, CPU | 7 passed |
| Same focused regressions, real Ascend NPU | 7 passed |
| Existing routing-simulator tests excluding model integration | 31 passed |
| Real NPU routing: 1/17/128 tokens, 128 experts, top-8; plain, grouped, biased, grouped sigmoid with bias | 12 comparisons; exact expert IDs and routing weights |
| Real NPU component construction | All 48 Qwen3 MoE layers use the three hooks; upstream factory remains intact |
| Explicit GPT-OSS expert loader and model runner on NPU, EPLB off/on | Exact loaded weights; constructor preserved; redundant expert slot allocated |
| Full applicable pre-commit hooks on changed files | Passed, including mypy 3.11 |

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_PLUGINS='' .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_routing.py -k 'platform_'
# In the Ascend environment, run the same pytest selection without forcing CPU.

VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_PLUGINS='' GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo0 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/kernels/moe/test_routing_simulator.py \
  -k 'not routing_strategy_integration'

pre-commit run --files vllm/platforms/interface.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/layer.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/router/router_factory.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_routing.py docs/design/plugin_system.md
```

The two parametrized model-component cases and the simulator hook case fail against the exact base (selected component type assertions), then pass with this change. The existing simulator model-integration test cannot select an unquantized backend for its CPU configuration on either base or head; it is not counted as passing.

Model-backed parity: Qwen3-30B-A3B BF16, TP=2/EP=2, Model Runner V2, ACL graph replay, seed 42, greedy decoding, prefix caching and chunked prefill disabled, synchronous scheduling and batch size 1. Across 10 requests / 320 generated tokens, the original Ascend factory patch and the hook consumer produced exactly identical token IDs and selected-token logprobs (maximum absolute difference 0). Each rank constructed all 48 MoE layers through all three hooks. This establishes output equivalence, not task accuracy: the baseline generations were not a quality-qualified reference.

The exploratory W8A8 runs are not reported as correctness passes: repeated original-patch baselines already differed for all 10 requests. This existing runtime/model quality and repeatability issue remains outside this construction-hook PR.

The NPU comparison uses a temporary Ascend hook consumer instead of the existing factory patch. Both arms use the same Ascend Python revision (`152444e7f63f36c8f9f3ef880654f14b01afdf98`) and prebuilt PyTorch 2.10/torch_npu 2.10 runtime. Two unrelated upstream API-drift points (adaptive verification and KV coordinator adaptation) are bypassed identically in this non-speculative validation fixture. No fixture changes are included in this PR. Full EPLB migration, other devices, and performance are not claimed as validated.

## Details

The platform receives the selected class at its construction boundary. Expert and runner adaptation happens after model-specific and expert-substitution selection. Router adaptation happens at each existing construction site, including the simulator wrapper after the real router has supplied its kernel routing method. Default implementations return the selected class. The platform remains responsible for preserving model loading and routing semantics.

AI assistance was used for implementation, review, validation scripts, and this description. This PR is ready for maintainer review. Human line-by-line review and maintainer acceptance remain required before merge.

cc @tlrmchlsmth — this adds three construction-time platform hooks (router / routed experts / runner) around the fused MoE factory path, which sits in the FusedMoE area you own (`docs/governance/committers.md`). Default platform behavior and upstream selection priority are unchanged; out-of-tree devices simply gain an adaptation point instead of replacing `FusedMoEFactory`. Happy to walk through the design whenever convenient.
✅ Queued 1 failed job(s) for retry in [Buildkite CI #99888](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99888).

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

I'm not opposed to some sort of plugin mechanism but I'm concerned that this one will break a number of existing places that already use custom classes, e.g.

 - vllm/model_executor/models/dbrx.py — DbrxExperts
  - vllm/model_executor/models/gpt_oss.py — GptOssRoutedExperts
  - vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/moe.py — TransformersRoutedExperts, TransformersMoERunner
  - vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/model.py — DeepseekV4HeterogeneousSharedRoutedExperts
  - vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/linear.py — ROCmLatentMoERunner
  - vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/model.py — LatentMoERunner
  - vllm/models/muse_spark/amd/model.py — MuseSparkRoutedExperts, MuseMoERunner
  - vllm/models/muse_spark/nvidia/model.py — MuseSparkRoutedExperts, MuseMoERunner
  - vllm/models/muse_spark/amd/model.py:268 — MuseSpark1xRouter
  - vllm/models/muse_spark/nvidia/model.py:647 — MuseSpark1xRouter

It seems like platform specific overrides would break one or more of these use cases.  It might make more sense if the platform provides a default rather than an override, so at least existing customizations will not break. I'm not sure of the best approach If custom classes need platform specific overrides.

files.patch:
@@ -106,6 +106,13 @@ Every plugin has three parts:
     - `get_attn_backend_cls`: This function should return the attention backend class's fully qualified name.
     - `get_device_communicator_cls`: This function should return the device communicator class's fully qualified name.
 
+    Platforms can also adapt fused MoE components during construction:
+
+    - `get_fused_moe_router_constructor(selected_cls)` returns a callable accepting the selected router branch's constructor arguments and producing a `FusedMoERouter`. A compatible sibling router is allowed. Preserve the selected branch's routing semantics and optional EPLB state.
+    - `get_fused_moe_routed_experts_cls(selected_cls)` and `get_fused_moe_runner_cls(selected_cls)` return `RoutedExperts` and `MoERunner` subclasses after the factory or model has selected its components. Preserve model-specific weight loading and execution behavior.
+
+    All three hooks return `selected_cls` by default. They run during construction, without changing factory selection priority or adding forward-time platform lookups. A router explicitly supplied to `FusedMoEFactory` is used directly. EPLB statistics, weight transfer, and commit ordering remain owned by EPLB.
+
 4. Implement the worker class `MyDummyWorker` in `my_dummy_worker.py`. The worker class should inherit from [WorkerBase][vllm.v1.worker.worker_base.WorkerBase]. Please follow the interface to implement the functions one by one. Basically, all interfaces in the base class should be implemented, since they are called here and there in vLLM. To make sure a model can be executed, the basic functions should be implemented are:
 
     - `init_device`: This function is called to set up the device for the worker.

@@ -6,12 +6,16 @@
 import pytest
 import torch
 
+import vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.layer as moe_layer
+import vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.router.router_factory as router_factory
 from vllm._aiter_ops import rocm_aiter_ops
+from vllm.config import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
 from vllm.distributed.eplb.eplb_state import EplbLayerState
 from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.config import RoutingMethodType
 from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.router.base_router import (
     eplb_map_to_physical_and_record,
 )
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.router.cpu_router import CPURouter
 from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.router.fused_topk_bias_router import (
     FusedTopKBiasRouter,
 )
@@ -24,8 +28,14 @@
 from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.router.router_factory import (
     create_fused_moe_router,
 )
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.router.routing_simulator_router import (
+    RoutingSimulatorRouter,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.runner.moe_runner import MoERunner
+from vllm.model_executor.models.gpt_oss import GptOssRoutedExperts
 from vllm.model_executor.models.llama4 import Llama4MoE
 from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.platforms.interface import Platform
 
 DEVICE = current_platform.device_type
 
@@ -95,6 +105,179 @@ def packed_routing(hidden_states, gating_output, topk, renormalize):
         router.select_experts(torch.empty((2, 8), device=DEVICE), routing)
 
 
+def test_platform_router_constructor_accepts_compatible_sibling() -> None:
+    def choose_constructor(selected_cls):
+        if selected_cls is FusedTopKRouter:
+            return lambda **kwargs: FusedTopKBiasRouter(**kwargs)
+        return selected_cls
+
+    with (
+        patch.object(current_platform, "is_cpu", return_value=False),
+        patch.object(
+            current_platform,
+            "get_fused_moe_router_constructor",
+            side_effect=choose_constructor,
+        ),
+    ):
+        router = create_fused_moe_router(top_k=2, global_num_experts=8)
+    assert isinstance(router, FusedTopKBiasRouter)
+
+
+def test_platform_router_constructor_rejects_non_router() -> None:
+    with (
+        patch.object(current_platform, "is_cpu", return_value=False),
+        patch.object(
+            current_platform,
+            "get_fused_moe_router_constructor",
+            return_value=lambda **kwargs: object(),
+        ),
+        pytest.raises(TypeError, match="must return FusedMoERouter"),
+    ):
+        create_fused_moe_router(top_k=2, global_num_experts=8)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("enable_eplb", [False, True])
+def test_platform_adapts_selected_fused_moe_components(monkeypatch, enable_eplb):
+    """Factory adaptation preserves model loading and the router's EPLB state."""
+
+    class PlatformRoutedExperts(GptOssRoutedExperts):
+        pass
+
+    class ModelRunner(MoERunner):
+        pass
+
+    class PlatformRunner(ModelRunner):
+        pass
+
+    class PlatformRouter(CPURouter):
+        pass
+
+    class TestPlatform(Platform):
+        _enum = current_platform._enum
+
+        @classmethod
+        def get_fused_moe_router_constructor(cls, selected_cls):
+            if selected_cls in (CPURouter, FusedTopKRouter):
+                return PlatformRouter
+            return selected_cls
+
+        @classmethod
+        def get_fused_moe_routed_experts_cls(cls, selected_cls):
+            return (
+                PlatformRoutedExperts
+                if selected_cls is GptOssRoutedExperts
+                else selected_cls
+            )
+
+        @classmethod
+        def get_fused_moe_runner_cls(cls, selected_cls):
+            return PlatformRunner if selected_cls is ModelRunner else selected_cls
+
+    platform = TestPlatform()
+    monkeypatch.setattr(moe_layer, "current_platform", platform, raising=False)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(router_factory, "current_platform", platform)
+    with set_current_vllm_config(VllmConfig()), torch.device(DEVICE):
+        runner = moe_layer.FusedMoEFactory(
+            num_experts=4,
+            top_k=2,
+            hidden_size=128,
+            intermediate_size=128,
+            params_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+            tp_size=1,
+            dp_size=1,
+            pcp_size=1,
+            routed_experts_cls=GptOssRoutedExperts,
+            runner_cls=ModelRunner,
+            enable_eplb=enable_eplb,
+            prefix="platform_components",
+        )
+    assert isinstance(runner, PlatformRunner)
+    assert isinstance(runner.router, PlatformRouter)
+    assert isinstance(runner.routed_experts, PlatformRoutedExperts)
+    assert (runner.eplb_state is not None) == enable_eplb
+
+    experts = runner.routed_experts
+    weight = experts.w13_weight
+    checkpoint_weight = torch.arange(
+        weight[0].numel(), dtype=weight.dtype, device=weight.device
+    ).reshape(weight.shape[2], weight.shape[1])
+    experts.weight_loader(
+        weight, checkpoint_weight, "w13_weight", "gpt_oss_w13", 0, return_success=False
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(weight[0], checkpoint_weight.t(), rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+def test_platform_simulator_preserves_selected_routing_method(monkeypatch):
+    class PlatformSimulator(RoutingSimulatorRouter):
+        pass
+
+    class TestPlatform(Platform):
+        _enum = current_platform._enum
+
+        @classmethod
+        def get_fused_moe_router_constructor(cls, selected_cls):
+            if selected_cls is RoutingSimulatorRouter:
+                return PlatformSimulator
+            return selected_cls
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(router_factory, "current_platform", TestPlatform())
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_MOE_ROUTING_SIMULATION_STRATEGY", "uniform_random")
+    state = EplbLayerState()
+    router = create_fused_moe_router(
+        top_k=4,
+        global_num_experts=128,
+        use_grouped_topk=True,
+        num_expert_group=8,
+        topk_group=4,
+        scoring_func="sigmoid",
+        e_score_correction_bias=torch.zeros(128),
+        eplb_state=state,
+    )
+    assert isinstance(router, PlatformSimulator)
+    assert router.kernel_routing_method_type == RoutingMethodType.DeepSeekV3
+    assert router.eplb_state is state
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("hook_name", "message"),
+    [
+        (
+            "get_fused_moe_routed_experts_cls",
+            "must return a RoutedExperts class",
+        ),
+        (
+            "get_fused_moe_runner_cls",
+            "must return a MoERunner class",
+        ),
+    ],
+)
+def test_platform_rejects_invalid_fused_moe_component_class(
+    monkeypatch, hook_name, message
+) -> None:
+    platform = type(
+        "InvalidPlatform",
+        (Platform,),
+        {hook_name: classmethod(lambda cls, selected_cls: object)},
+    )()
+    monkeypatch.setattr(moe_layer, "current_platform", platform)
+    with (
+        set_current_vllm_config(VllmConfig()),
+        torch.device(DEVICE),
+        pytest.raises(TypeError, match=message),
+    ):
+        moe_layer.FusedMoEFactory(
+            num_experts=4,
+            top_k=2,

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

I'm not opposed to some sort of plugin mechanism but I'm concerned that this one will break a number of existing places that already use custom classes, e.g.

 - vllm/model_executor/models/dbrx.py — DbrxExperts
  - vllm/model_executor/models/gpt_oss.py — GptOssRoutedExperts
  - vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/moe.py — TransformersRoutedExperts, TransformersMoERunner
  - vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/model.py — DeepseekV4HeterogeneousSharedRoutedExperts
  - vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/linear.py — ROCmLatentMoERunner
  - vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/model.py — LatentMoERunner
  - vllm/models/muse_spark/amd/model.py — MuseSparkRoutedExperts, MuseMoERunner
  - vllm/models/muse_spark/nvidia/model.py — MuseSparkRoutedExperts, MuseMoERunner
  - vllm/models/muse_spark/amd/model.py:268 — MuseSpark1xRouter
  - vllm/models/muse_spark/nvidia/model.py:647 — MuseSpark1xRouter

It seems like platform specific overrides would break one or more of these use cases.  It might make more sense if the platform provides a default rather than an override, so at least existing customizations will not break. I'm not sure of the best approach If custom classes need platform specific overrides.
